dialogue.text: Pricing agreements in, invoices out, and a validator in between that doesn't trust either. It's a nice story when you draw it on a whiteboard.
Byron's in the corner office. Say hi to Numair first, he has news. There is always news.
Martin. New York suits you. Applied science on billing. Not glamorous, very expensive when it's wrong.
The pricing-agreement validator is finding real bugs now. Safe Validation of Pricing Agreements, ICSE '25. Reviewers asked how much money. We couldn't say.
And the bill explainer learned its rules from documentation. 'Why Is This on My Bill?', ICSE '26. Finally a title my mother understands.
Byron wants you in his office. Talk to the team first; they'll want to show off.
Go talk to Byron! And then go have brunch with Lauren. It's the weekend. Probably.
Martin! 😄 The contract parser broke again. Not my fault. Well. Partly my fault.
The delta debugging paper got in! ICSE '26. Shrink an LLM pipeline failure down to the one input that breaks it. Very satisfying. Very slow.
And the region paper with Tancrède and Liana: turn a yes/no question over a rule engine into a region and let a solver answer it. NeSy liked it.
Now go see Byron. He's been pacing.
Office Michael is different from street Michael. Office Michael has a standing desk.
Rapid became the API-usage checks in CodeGuru Reviewer. Static analysis for everyone, in the cloud, with a paper to prove it.
CodeGuru, CodeWhisperer, Kiro. We built a lot of developer tools before the whole 'reasoning about agents' thing. Byron's office is top right.
Martin. You've met the team. Pricing agreements, bill explanations, agents voting on agents. Billing was the warm-up.
Here's the thing. I need someone who's seen the whole stack, from loops in Freiburg to invoices in Manhattan.
Advise me. Shadow me. Help me run Automated Reasoning across AWS. Proofs, Lean, agents, all of it.
That's the spirit. Welcome to the next chapter.
Take your time. There are still papers lying around the office.
Martin! Good, you found the place. Go say hi to Willem and Numair first. Then we talk.
